methods_proposed.name: Linear Regression
methods_proposed.description: Simple linear model predicting Sales from advertising features
methods_proposed.implementation_code:
def predict_linear_regression(train_df, test_df, target_col, **params):
    from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
    from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
    import pandas as pd
    
    model = LinearRegression()
    model.fit(train_df[['TV', 'Radio', 'Newspaper']], train_df[target_col])
    predictions = model.predict(test_df[['TV', 'Radio', 'Newspaper']])
    return pd.DataFrame({'predicted': predictions}, index=test_df.index)

def predict_ridge_regression(train_df, test_df, target_col, **params):
    from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge
    from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
    import pandas as pd
    
    model = Ridge(alpha=1.0)
    model.fit(train_df[['TV', 'Radio', 'Newspaper']], train_df[target_col])
    predictions = model.predict(test_df[['TV', 'Radio', 'Newspaper']])
    return pd.DataFrame({'predicted': predictions}, index=test_df.index)

def predict_random_forest(train_df, test_df, target_col, **params):
    from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
    from sklearn.metrics import mean_squared_error
    import pandas as pd
    
    model = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)
    model.fit(train_df[['TV', 'Radio', 'Newspaper']], train_df[target_col])
    predictions = model.predict(test_df[['TV', 'Radio', 'Newspaper']])
    return pd.DataFrame({'predicted': predictions}, index=test_df.index)
